deepdive.divline: Rights Issue of INR 364cr planned for R-32 plant; Promoter to subscribe proportionately (including conversion of interest-free loan); No further equity dilution expected post-rights; Debt-free stance maintained
deepdive.netdebt: Debt-free (Promoter injected interest-free loan for R-32 kickstart)

profile.entities: Stallion India Fluorochemicals Ltd; SYS Advanced (Portugal); Sharjah Oxygen (Dubai)
profile.subseg: Refrigerant Gases (HFC/HFO); Helium & Specialty Gases; High-Purity Industrial Applications
profile.themes: R-32 Backward Integration; Helium Supply Chain Resilience; Capacity Scale-up

bull_bear.body: Rights Issue of INR 364cr planned for R-32 plant; Promoter to subscribe proportionately (including conversion of interest-free loan); No further equity dilution expected post-rights; Debt-free stance maintained.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) Commissioning delays (Khalapur helium delayed 3 months due to pressure upgrade to 300 bar; Mambatu re-engineered for larger scale); 2) Execution risk on rapid capex deployment; 3) Raw material volatility (imported helium/components); 4) Regulatory changes in fluorocarbons.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term structural shift to manufacturing; Defensive on communication gaps regarding delays (cites 're-engineering' for better economics); Aggressive on margin expansion and market share capture.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Promoter's 2% stake sale was a bridge to fund R-32 kickstart after market volatility killed a preferential issue; R-32 capacity doubled mid-stream (5k to 10k MT) to avoid future shutdowns for expansion, signaling a 'big bang' manufacturing entry rather than phased learning.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Refrigerants: R-32 backward integration (10k MT Bhilwara); Specialty Gases: Helium liquefaction/recovery (Khalapur & Mambatu), HFO blending; High-Purity: Semiconductor/Defense applications via SYS Advanced tie-up.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Import dependency for R-32 and high-purity helium; volatile logistics costs. | Stallion India Fluorochemicals Ltd | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of backward integration; moving from trading margins to manufacturing margins (10% -> 24% PAT). |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Specialized, 30+ year player in refrigerant/industrial gas debulking, blending and processing, holding sizeable market share in India with 200+ customers across 15+ industry segments.
- Strategic partnerships with Honeywell (HFC/fluorine/refrigerant-specialty distribution; Solstice HFO refrigerants) and Daikin Japan/India (HFC-32 sourcing and logistics) underpin market access.
- Emphasizes aftermarket clients, which management says make up 80% of the total addressable market and deliver substantially higher margins than OEM customers, as a core differentiator.
- Diversified, pan-India customer base and long-term relationships are cited as reducing dependence on any single end-market.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Guidance] Chairman's letter and Way Forward section state management expects 30-35% revenue CAGR over the next 3 years while maintaining sustainable margins, and targets a ~3-4% EBITDA/profitability margin improvement over the medium term from backward integration and higher-value products (e.g., semiconductor gases) - explicitly flagged by the deck as forward-looking, not established fact.
- [Helium sourcing deal] Long-term strategic sourcing partnership with Sharjah Oxygen Company L.L.C. (SOC), sourcing liquid helium from RAS Gases & Oilfields, Qatar, targets semiconductor/electronics, healthcare (MRI/medical imaging), aerospace & defense, and fiber-optics end markets.
- [Industry sizing, third-party sources] Deck cites the global fluorochemicals market at USD 76.7bn (2025) growing to USD 204.4bn by 2035 (10.3% CAGR, Future Market Insights) and the India fluorochemicals market at ~USD 750mn (2025) growing at ~10.5% CAGR through 2034 (marknteladvisors/Thereportcubes) - external estimates, not company data.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Current PAT margin ~10%; Target PAT margin 24% for new products (R-32, Helium); Cost competitiveness via backward integration and economies of scale (doubled R-32 capacity from 5k to 10k MT).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: FY26 Revenue: INR 430cr; FY26 PAT: INR 40cr; Margin Target: 24% PAT (up from current ~10%) driven by new products; CAGR Target: 30-35% over next 3 years.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not explicitly quantified; Management cites 200+ customers across 15 countries; R-32 plant expected to contribute INR 275cr revenue in first 6 months (Oct '26-Mar '27).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) R-32 captive production (10k MT) replacing imports; 2) Helium network expansion (West/South India) targeting INR 200cr revenue in 5 years; 3) Future HFO plant post-R-32 commissioning; 4) By-product commercialization.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Stallion is transitioning from a blender/distributor to an integrated manufacturer with a 10k MT R-32 plant (Aug '26) and expanded helium infrastructure, targeting a PAT margin jump from 10% to 24%. While FY26 guidance (INR 430cr Rev, INR 40cr PAT) remains intact, execution risks on capex funding (Rights Issue) and plant commissioning delays (Khalapur/Mambatu to Mar-Apr '26) are key near-term monitors.
